clue.text: Inscriptions not the happiest — yet they could be

indicators.note: the letters of happiest could be rearranged into something else, the clue says; that hint of possible transformation signals an anagram

explanation.surface: Gravestone wording is rarely cheerful, though the setter teases that it might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not the happiest' reads as a comment on gravestones; really 'happiest' is the fodder and 'could be' says its letters could become the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Words carved on a tomb in memory of the dead are a kind of inscription.

clue.text: Press for identity documents?

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to produce proof of who they are.
explanation.definitionFit: The press is a collective word for newspapers, and identity documents are also commonly called by the same plural word.

clue.text: Small bird and an enormous one

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tiny bird is paired with a giant one, like a wren beside an ostrich.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titans were giants, so the word is used for anything or anyone huge.

clue.text: New blow follows strike, leading to depression in the land

indicators.note: the new piece comes after the strike piece, so it is placed second

parts.note: to strike is to punch

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters of blow are remade in a new order

explanation.surface: A boxer lands another blow after a first strike, knocking the opponent down.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxing surface makes 'depression' sound like a knocked-down fighter's mood; it is a hollow in the landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl-shaped hollow in hills or landscape is called by this name, a geographical term for a basin.

clue.text: Disposes of everything, gets a higher price

definitions.meaning: sells all of one's business or property
sells for more, read literally as selling upwards

explanation.surface: A trader clears out all stock and makes a profit doing so.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means selling off one's whole business, and read literally it means selling at a raised price.

clue.text: Unexpected opportunity

definitions.meaning: an opening, a possibility to do something

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means accidental or unforeseen; as a noun it means an opening or occasion to act.

clue.text: Figures it's only one among 100s

indicators.note: the single piece is set in the midst of the hundreds, so it goes inside them

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, so two of them give CS
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a single item is lost amid hundreds of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' looks like numbers, fitting 100s, but means solid shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone is a solid geometric shape, and such shapes are called figures in geometry.

clue.text: Reptile perturbs a girl a lot

indicators.note: to perturb is to throw into disorder, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A frightening reptile thoroughly upsets a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: This large toothed animal of American and Chinese rivers is a reptile related to the crocodile.

clue.text: Fifty joining in in carol with shaking bells

indicators.note: the pieces are shaken up together, so their letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fifty people join in a carol while bells ring out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With shaking' mixes L, IN and CAROL together; the first 'in' and 'joining' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of tuned bells in a tower, played from a keyboard, is known by this name.

clue.text: First-class returns operating, excellent!

indicators.note: returning means the word for first-class is read backwards

parts.note: the tops means the very best, first-class
a machine that is operating is switched on

explanation.surface: A first-class service comes back into operation, to applause.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation means exactly right or perfect, an informal expression of approval.

clue.text: Letter providing you with accommodation

parts.note: a letter here is not a written message but one who lets property to tenants

explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like correspondence about housing, but it means someone who lets.
explanation.definitionFit: The owner who rents out rooms or a house is one who lets, so a letter in the punning sense.

clue.text: Subsidiary parts of the Forestry Commission?

definitions.text: Subsidiary parts of the Forestry Commission?

parts.words: Subsidiary parts of the Forestry Commission?
parts.note: local offices of an organisation are also the limbs of trees, which a forestry body tends

explanation.walkthrough: The Forestry Commission is the British government body managing state forests; its local offices share a name with tree limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Local offices of an organisation are its subsidiary divisions, and trees also have these limbs.

clue.text: Shrewdly canny about how old one is

indicators.note: the canny word goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a canny or cunning person is sly
your age is how old you are

explanation.surface: Someone is cagey and clever when asked their age.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something wisely and with good judgement is acting in a sage manner, the adverb of sage.

clue.text: An actor may take it when at a loss for words

definitions.text: An actor may take it when at a loss for words

parts.words: An actor may take it when at a loss for words
parts.note: an actor who forgets lines is given a prompt, and acting quickly is the other reading

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means quick action; here it is a cue from the prompter given to an actor who dries.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual idiom means swift decisive steps, but punningly it is action prompted from the wings.

clue.text: Share pusher

parts.note: a share is the blade of a plough, and one who pushes it is a farm worker; the surface suggests a stock tout

explanation.walkthrough: 'Share pusher' suggests someone hawking stocks; a ploughshare is the cutting blade of a plough.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm worker who guides a plough drives its cutting blade, the share, through the soil.

clue.text: Lending is increasing

definitions.meaning: making an advance, paying money ahead as a loan
moving forward or rising, as prices advance

explanation.surface: A bank observer notes that lending is on the rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance money is to lend it, and prices advancing are going up.

clue.text: Tapping cacao led to blend

indicators.note: blending mixes things together, so the letters of the fodder are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe step: cocoa beans are used in making a blend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tapping' suggests tapping a tree for sap; it refers to the touch on the shoulder with a sword in knighting.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial touch of a sword on the shoulder when conferring knighthood was the original sense of this honour.

clue.text: He loves Carol madly, but she won't be in form much longer

definitions.text: she won't be in form much longer

indicators.note: loving madly suggests wild disorder, so the letters are wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: A schoolboy is besotted with a classmate who is about to finish school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' is a British school class, not shape or fitness.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil in the final school year will soon leave and no longer belong to any class or form.

clue.text: Lands in eastern America

parts.note: the States is a common name for the USA

explanation.surface: Property holdings located on America's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Large landed properties with houses and grounds are estates, a synonym for lands owned.

clue.text: He doesn't think much of others

definitions.text: He doesn't think much of others

parts.words: He doesn't think much of others
parts.note: someone selfish who thinks chiefly of himself rather than other people

explanation.definitionFit: A self-centred person preoccupied with his own interests gives little thought to anyone else.

clue.text: Bottle opener needs to be purchased

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ought to be means needs to be, should be

explanation.surface: A bottle opener must be bought before the wine can be enjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle opener' reads as a corkscrew; 'opener' takes just the first letter of 'Bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something acquired by paying for it has been bought, the past participle of buy.

clue.text: One of five that's unaccountable

definitions.meaning: from the saying that there is no accounting for preferences

explanation.surface: One out of five items defies any explanation.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition alludes to the proverb 'there's no accounting for taste'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the five senses, and personal preference is proverbially impossible to account for.

clue.text: Some guys become attached to them

definitions.text: Some guys become attached to them

parts.words: Some guys become attached to them
parts.note: guys are the ropes holding a tent, tied to stakes in the ground; the surface suggests men growing fond

explanation.walkthrough: 'Guys' suggests men forming attachments; guy ropes are tied to the stakes holding a tent down.
explanation.definitionFit: Stakes driven into the ground anchor the ropes, called guys, that keep a tent upright.

clue.text: Vegetables that a sister will take

definitions.meaning: edible seeds of legumes such as lentils and beans
a nurse takes a patient's heartbeat rate; in Britain a sister is a senior nurse

explanation.surface: A nun or sibling is offered some vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'sister' is a senior hospital nurse, who checks a patient's heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentils, peas and beans are edible seeds called by this name, and the rhythmic heartbeat felt at the wrist shares it.

clue.text: Market in which you will see some strange animal

indicators.note: the market word holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a mart is a market

indicators.note: strange suggests something altered and odd, so the letters of some are rearranged

explanation.surface: A market where shoppers come across an odd creature for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You will see' is padding between the container signal 'in which' and the anagram; 'strange' looks like it describes the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This small long-tailed South American monkey is a specific kind of animal.

clue.text: Like marquetry with fashionable styling of Dali

parts.note: something fashionable is in

indicators.note: styling reshapes something, so the letters of the painter's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Decorative wood veneer work done in the trendy style of the surrealist painter Dali.
explanation.definitionFit: Marquetry is decoration of pieces of veneer set into a surface, so it is work of this set-in kind.

clue.text: Occasion when spirits are called for

definitions.text: Occasion when spirits are called for

parts.words: Occasion when spirits are called for
parts.note: spirits suggests ordering drinks at a bar, but here it is ghosts summoned by a medium

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits are called for' suggests ordering drinks; it means summoning the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering where a medium tries to contact the dead is a meeting at which ghosts are summoned.

clue.text: Gems sent out in parcels

indicators.note: the letters are put out of their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jewels are posted off in packages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parcels' looks like packages but is a verb, as in parcelling out land.
explanation.definitionFit: To parcel something is to divide it into portions, a verb synonym for splitting into sections.
